newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DAX index sets sight on breaking 4,000.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DAX index sets sight on breaking 4,000.

text.p: Germany's DAX index set its sights on breaking 4,000 points in the coming weeks after the blue-chip index surged to another new record high on Thursday in pre-bourse IBIS computer dealings.
The IBIS DAX was up 4.43 points at 3,871.27 points after setting a new record high at 3,892.18 and surpassing the last all-time record at 3,870.81 points set on Wednesday.

But traders said profit-taking has set in ahead of the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. jobless data for May as the German market waits for the report's impact on U.S. financial markets ahead of the Independence Day long holiday weekend.
"The market is well-bid and the DAX could very well reach 3,900 today," said one Frankfurt trader. "But investors are going to be cautious, so I expect some more consolidation."
Overnight Wall Street gains, where the Dow Jones index surged about one percent to 7,795.38 points, and the dollar traded above 1.75 marks were the main factors driving the DAX.
The higher dollar was underpinning export-sensitive shares, particularly in the chemical and automotive sectors, as traders said the DAX could break 4,000 points in the next few weeks.
"The ace in the pack is how the U.S. jobs data comes out today," said a Frankfurt share trader.
"The problem, however, is that the market is in blue skies, so it is hard to say where the gains should stop. We could see 4,000 points fairly soon," the trader said.

Chemical shares, which were at the market forefront earlier in the week, were generally lower on profit-taking following recent sharp gains. But traders said the sector was still in vogue and that the uptrend would resume in the near-term.
Hoechst AG, which has risen more than 10 percent since June 25, was down 40 pfennigs at 78.30 marks, while Bayer AG was down 55 pfennigs at 70.30 marks and BASF AG fell 45 pfennigs to 65.65 marks.
Bank shares were mixed as Deutche Bank AG slipped five pfennigs to 104.50 marks after setting another new record high at 105.35 marks in initial dealings.
Daimler-Benz AG was down 40 pfennigs at 145.30 marks after also setting a new record high at 146.20 marks.
But other carmakers were higher, including Volkswagen AG that was up 6.25 marks at 1,363.50 marks and BMW AG that gained up 8.40 marks at 1,452.90 marks.
Porsche, another top gainer in recent weeks, was up 15 marks at 2,530 marks. Brokerage house Lehman said this week it set a price target for Porsche at 3,600 marks.
